scenarios.title: DynamoDB GetItem, throttled twice, then OK
scenarios.what: Default retry policy. Operation mode records the retries on the one span (attempts, error of each failed try, total backoff); debug mode shows each try as an Attempt span with serialize, sign and the HTTP request under it, and the backoff sleeps between them.

scenarios.title: S3 PutObject, SlowDown ×4 (≈ 4.4 s)
scenarios.what: A call that took about 4.4 s. The operation span alone shows why: distilled.attempts is 5, distilled.retry.errors lists 4 SlowDown responses, and distilled.retry.delay_ms is about 4 s of backoff. Debug mode shows each try as its own span.

scenarios.title: SQS SendMessage
scenarios.what: A PRODUCER span named after the messaging conventions, send {queue}. It writes its own W3C trace context into the message as the traceparent message attribute (see the request sent), so the receiver can link back to it.

scenarios.title: SQS ReceiveMessage → link to producer
scenarios.what: The receive span asks SQS for the traceparent message attribute and links to the producer span of every message it gets, so a trace shows send → receive. The span name follows the messaging conventions: receive {queue}.

scenarios.title: R2 through the S3 SDK
scenarios.what: S3.getObject against an R2 endpoint. The S3 host rule records the Cloudflare attributes the Cloudflare SDK's R2 operations record (cloudflare.account_id, cloudflare.r2.bucket, cloudflare.r2.object_key) and R2's cf-ray, so both paths to one bucket line up.

scenarios.title: R2 through the Cloudflare SDK
scenarios.what: The same bucket through Cloudflare's REST API: Cloudflare.GetBucket with the same cloudflare.account_id and cloudflare.r2.bucket as the S3 path.

scenarios.title: Railway GraphQL document
scenarios.what: Railway's Query client sends one GraphQL document; it gets one span, named by its root field, with graphql.operation.* and the ids from its arguments.

scenarios.title: Stripe GetCustomer → 404
scenarios.what: Stripe's own protocol (form-encoded, its error envelope). The span carries Stripe's request-id, the id Stripe support asks for, and the customer id from the path.

scenarios.title: GCP Cloud Storage objects.get
scenarios.what: A Google discovery API. Each GCP API is its own product, so the span is named by the service (Storage.GetObjects), and the bucket and object come from the path.

scenarios.title: Azure GetResourceGroup
scenarios.what: An Azure Resource Manager call. Azure's request ids (x-ms-request-id, x-ms-correlation-request-id) land on the span, with the subscription and resource group from the path.

scenarios.title: GitHub repos.get
scenarios.what: GitHub's REST API. The span is GitHub.Get with owner and repo from the path and GitHub's x-github-request-id.

scenarios.title: Neon getProject
scenarios.what: A plain OpenAPI provider on the shared REST protocol: Neon.GetProject with neon.project_id from the path.

scenarios.title: Vercel getProject
scenarios.what: Vercel's REST API: vercel.id_or_name from the path and Vercel's x-vercel-id.

scenarios.title: Slack chat.postMessage → ok: false
scenarios.what: Slack answers 200 with ok: false. The span still ends as an error with the typed tag, and carries Slack's x-slack-req-id.

scenarios.title: Fly.io Machines getApp
scenarios.what: Fly's Machines REST API: Fly.GetApp with fly_io.app_name and Fly's fly-request-id.

scenarios.title: Bedrock Converse (GenAI)
scenarios.what: A GenAI client span per the GenAI conventions: chat {model}, the request's model and inference settings, and the response's token usage and finish reason. The request also carries an X-Amzn-Trace-Id header.

scenarios.title: Lambda Invoke
scenarios.what: The function's trace context goes in ClientContext (base64 JSON, custom.traceparent), where the invoked function reads it; faas.invoked_region comes from the call's region.

scenarios.title: EventBridge PutEvents
scenarios.what: No messaging conventions cover EventBridge, so this stays an AWS SDK span (EventBridge.PutEvents), as a producer, and writes an X-Ray TraceHeader into every entry.

scenarios.title: Cloudflare listZones, 3 pages
scenarios.what: A paginated stream. Every page is one operation call, so one operation span each.
